history.change: Initial draft, before any data was labeled.

After a 312-message pilot (61 mistakes): 'other' was the largest type (15), made of answers that missed the question, unclear or overlong reports, and wrong facts, so each became its own type. 'asked-too-little' was confused with 'asked-too-much' and was renamed 'acted-without-asking' with a narrower definition. 'false-claim' now covers only claims about the agent's own work.

categories.title: Ignored instruction
categories.definition: The agent did not do something the user explicitly asked for in this session, or did the opposite, so the user has to repeat or restate it.

categories.title: False or overstated claim of result
categories.definition: The agent said its own work was done, fixed, verified, sent or passing, and the user found it was not, or only partly.

categories.title: Wrong fact or unchecked assumption
categories.definition: The agent stated or acted on a wrong fact, name, identifier, number or assumption about the system or the situation that it could have checked.

categories.title: Unnecessary work
categories.definition: The agent did work nobody asked for: extra features, files, refactors, long output, or a heavier process than the task needed.

categories.title: Asked too much
categories.definition: The agent stopped to ask, confirm, or hand a step back to the user when it had the information, access and permission to do it itself.

categories.title: Acted without asking
categories.definition: The agent took, or was about to take, a consequential or hard-to-undo action, or settled an ambiguous point by guessing, without the user's go-ahead.

categories.title: Broke something that worked
categories.definition: The agent's change broke working code, data, configuration or a running system, or lost the user's work.

categories.title: Ignored repository or standing rules
categories.definition: The agent broke a rule from the project's instruction files, a skill, memory, or an established team process.

categories.title: Wrong tool or approach
categories.definition: The agent chose an unsuitable tool, method, design or place to work when a better one was available or already named.

categories.title: Missed the question
categories.definition: The agent answered a different question, misread what the user meant, or left the actual question unanswered, so the user had to ask again.

categories.title: Unclear or overlong report
categories.definition: The agent's answer or status report was too long, confusing, full of jargon, or missed the key point, so the user could not tell what happened or what to do.

categories.title: Other
categories.definition: A clear agent mistake that fits none of the categories above. Give a 2-4 word name in other_label.
